newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan hikes security for slain Iranians funeral.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan hikes security for slain Iranians funeral.

text.p: Pakistan tightened security in the city of Multan on Friday for the funerals of five of eight people killed in an attack on an Iranian cultural centre, witnesses said.

Officials said the body of the Iranian director of the centre, Muhammad Ali Rahimi, and his family had been flown to Tehran from Multan on a Pakistan Air Force plane, accompanied by Mushahid Hussain, an aide to new Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif.
Several gunmen attacked the centre in Multan, in southern Punjab province, on Thursday, killing Rahimi and seven Pakistanis, including a policeman and a civilian guard.
Police were out in force to keep order during the funerals, expected to draw big crowds after Friday prayers.

The Iranian consulate-general in the Punjab capital Lahore blamed "anti-Islamic agents of world imperialism" for the shooting, which Shi'ite Moslem groups have said was the work of the militant Sunni Moslem Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan (SSP) group.
Allama Sajid Naqvi, leader of the Shi'ite Tehrik-i-Jafria Pakistan (TJP) group, said the attack was part of a conspiracy by anti-Islamic forces opposed to Pakistani-Iranian cooperation.

A Foreign Ministry spokesman said Pakistan would not let anyone disrupt its ties with Iran. "Whatever the motivations of the perpetrators, we will never allow anyone to disrupt our time-tested and fraternal relations with Iran," he said.
Punjab police said on Thursday they had made some arrests after the attack, but gave no details.
On January 19, SSP supporters burned the Iranian cultural centre in Lahore a day after a bomb blast there killed their leader Zia-ur-Rahman Faruqi and 25 other people.
SSP followers blamed Shi'ite militants for the bombing. SSP deputy leader Azam Tariq was among about 90 wounded.
A long-running feud between Sunni and Shi'ite militants killed at least 170 people last year in Pakistan, where Shi'ites make up about 15 percent of the population of 131 million.
Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati is expected to visit Pakistan next week to deliver invitations for an Islamic summit conference to be held in Tehran in December.
Shi'ite-majority Iran has in the past urged Pakistan to protect Shi'ites from attacks by what it calls terrorists.
